title: Thermostat Autoscale + Graceful Throttle prototype (PRD draft)
body:
TL;DR:
Small prototype PRD for a "thermostat" style autoscaler that actively modulates burst allowances and throttling intensity to keep latency SLOs stable while minimizing reserved-capacity waste. Combines a short-window burst-credit allocator, a proactive prewarm/priming signal, and a graceful-throttle controller that degrades QoS predictably (soft vs hard limits). Goal: reduce peak reserved delta by ~20% without increasing P99 > 10% on gold-tier tenants.

Context / problem:
- Dedicated pools are underutilized at night and highly peaky during business hours for many tenants. Current options (hard burst credits, static prewarm pools) are brittle and either waste capacity or produce sharp throttles that break UX.
- We need a control that can: smooth spikes, allow short microbursts, and gracefully step down heavy noisy tenants without global impact.

Hypothesis:
- A PID-ish "thermostat" controller that adjusts an effective burst budget and throttle slope based on observed latency, queue length, and recent token drain will keep SLOs stable and reduce reserved headroom. Add a lightweight proactive prewarm pump triggered by sustained ascent in short-window QPS to reduce cold-start penalties for predictable bursts.

Goals (measurable):
- Reduce average reserved headroom across sample tenants by 15–25% (simulated workloads).
- Hold P95 latency within current baseline +/-5% for gold SLO tenants during tests; P99 allowed up to +10% transiently with automated rollback.
- Provide transparent tenant-facing signals (remaining burst-credit, throttle-mode) via API/console.

Non-goals:
- This PRD does NOT replace long-term capacity marketplace mechanics or billing model changes. Not tackling preemptive cross-pool migrations here.

Design overview:
1) Thermostat controller:
   - Inputs: short-window P50/P95/P99 latencies, token drain rate, queue depth, recent prewarm events, dedicated pool utilization.
   - Outputs: per-tenant "burst budget" (time-decaying credit), throttle slope parameter (how quickly qps is reduced once credit depleted), prewarm trigger score.
   - Control loop frequency: 5s control ticks (configurable). Hysteresis windows to prevent oscillation.
   - Safety caps: absolute hard throttle that preserves system stability (global emergency cutoff).

2) Burst-budget model:
   - Credits accrue slowly when utilization < target baseline; credits spent when token drain exceeds steady-state cadence.
   - Two time constants: microburst (30s window) and macro smoothing (10m window). Separate pools to allow short high-QPS bursts but prevent long sustained steal.

3) Prewarm/Priming:
   - Predictive prewarm that can spin up warm workers (or move tenancy weight) when short-window slope and token-velocity indicate an upcoming surge.
   - Configurable aggressiveness per tenant (enterprise customers can opt into aggressive prewarm).

4) Graceful throttle modes:
   - Soft-throttle: gradual increase in latency-inducing backpressure (reduce concurrency, increase batching) to keep requests served but slower.
   - Hard-throttle: reject or queue beyond SLA threshold when system risk high.
   - Mode transitions logged and surfaced as events.

Tenant isolation interactions:
- Thermostat runs per-tenant within a pool but reads global pool state. This keeps noisy neighbor mitigation local while still protecting pool SLOs.
- If a tenant repeatedly hits hard-throttle, escalation paths: temporary quarantine (reduce burst accrual), notify SE/CS, recommend Dedicated plan adjustments.

API / Console exposure:
- New route: GET /v1/dedicated/tenants/{id}/burst-status -> returns human-friendly strings: {mode, credit_pct, window_remaining, last_prewarm}
- Console: per-tenant timeline, heatmap of burst events, recommended reservation delta.

Metrics / telemetry (minimum):
- Per-tenant: burst_credit_level, thermostat_mode, throttle_slope, prewarm_actions, reserve_headroom_delta.
- Pool-level: control-loop activations, emergency-cut events, aggregate headroom.

Simulated scenarios (plan):
- Spike (10x qps for 30s): expect microburst credit to cover 80% of cases with P99 within +5%.
- Sustained surge (10x for 10m): thermostat should deplete macro credit, shift into soft-throttle, and signal prewarm early; P95 within +10% acceptable.
- Noisy neighbor: one tenant cycles bursts every 2m; thermostat should prevent long-term resource domination and quarantine after policies.

Safety / fallback:
- Rollback path: global switch to "fixed credit" mode (current behavior) via ops console.
- Canary: enable thermostat for 5 tenants in a pool, observe 48–72h, then expand.
- Alerting: immediate paging if emergency-cut triggered or P99 exceeds safety threshold for >5min.

Operational considerations:
- Controller must be lightweight (written in serving runtime agent or sidecar) and deterministic across restarts.
- Persist credit state with short TTL to avoid long-lived state corruption; store in pool-local KV with versioning.
- Explainability: telemetry + short human-readable rationale string for each mode transition (e.g., "fast-drain detected -> hard-cap applied").

Rollout plan (sketch):
- Week 0: unit tests + simulation harness (owners: Marco)
- Week 2: runtime integration in canary cluster, limited tenants (owners: Priya + runtime)
- Week 3–4: expand to 10% pools, real-traffic shadow testing (no throttle, just telemetry)
- Week 6: soft-throttle enabled for low-risk tenants, monitor metrics for 2 weeks
- Week 8+: assess cost savings and SLO impact, decide scale-up.

Open questions / risks:
- How to map burst-credit accounting to billing (billed tokens vs virtual credit)? (TODO: sync with finance — Aisha)
- Interaction with Dedicated reservation rebalancer: will thermostat cause churn? Need simulation with decommit flows.
- Edge-case: highly periodic traffic exactly aligned with macro window could game credits. Add entropy/randomized jitter to accrual.

Action items:
- [RED-4591] set up simulation scenarios + baseline (Marco)
- Implement minimal control loop prototype in runtime/sidecar (Priya)
- Design console UI mock for tenant signals (Evan)
- Draft customer-facing FAQ for enterprise beta (Aisha)

Notes / links:
- Slack thread: #eng-dedicated (see pinned: "thermostat-controller-discussion")
- Related RFC: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=987654321

Status: rough draft. Looking for early feedback on control frequency, credit time-constants, and recommended safe thresholds. Please drop comments inline or ping in #eng-dedicated.

-- Evan
